newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to slash wholesale gas price by 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia to slash wholesale gas price by 40 pct.

text.p: Russia will slash tariffs on wholesale natural gas supplied by Gazprom to domestic industrial users by 40 percent soon, Interfax news agency quoted Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov as saying on Wednesday.

"Soon a decree will be signed by President Boris Yeltsin on lowering Gazprom's tariffs on wholesale gas supplied to industry (in Russia) by 40 percent," Interfax said, attributing the remarks to Nemtsov.
Nemtsov was speaking at a meeting with deputies of the lower parliament State Duma, the agency said.

Nemtsov, also First Deputy Prime Minister, has been charged with re-vamping Russia's so-called "natural monopolies", including the gas industry, which is almost totally controlled by the world's biggest gas company, Gazprom.
It was not immediately clear what proportion of Gazprom's supplies to domestic industry was represented by the wholesale gas market.

The proposed cut in industrial wholesale gas prices will be welcome by industries across the country, many of which are still burdened by mounting debts both to other companies like Gazprom and to the federal budget.
